evidence: Line 15: “the systems that sit behind a Microsoft account stopped too”; line 23: “A backup chat keeps people talking but does not reopen those systems”. services.json line 10: “The impacts are partial: Teams core calls, meetings and chat are said to work, and SharePoint direct file access is said to work. The honest label is impacted, not down.” services.json line 256 (disagreement 6): “Microsoft names no Entra or sign-in service failure in any 12 to 13 Nov incident I read” and “Sign-in as a symptom is Microsoft-backed; sign-in as a failed service is not”. Lines 184-190 add a weak, anonymous report that single sign-on still worked for apps outside Microsoft 365. Line 55: “In Microsoft's wording the Exchange outage caused the sign-in failures, not the other way round.” Disagreement 4 (line 256): the shared-authentication framing and the core-authentication-configuration root cause “both belong to the 31 Aug to 3 Sep outage (EX1464935/MO1465074)”. The design's own line 32 forbids “down” and line 46 forbids saying sign-in went down, yet the thesis says “stopped”. The sweep does not bear out the owner's premise for this outage (brainstorm line 21, “since the login depend on them”; line 25, “when the Microsoft login stops”), and the design never tells the owner so. Instead it silently swaps “login” for “account” (lines 15, 23, 32), which drops the owner's word but keeps the claim that identity failed.
fix: Before drafting, put the conflict to the owner as a multiple-choice question. In Microsoft's record the wider impact runs through Exchange Online's connection systems, not through sign-in, and the login mechanism fits the 31 Aug outage. Rewrite the thesis and the turn so the systems are “listed by Microsoft as impacted” (partial impact on features that depend on Exchange Online). State the login point as the owner's general concern, not as what happened on 12 November. Avoid “Microsoft account” as the shared door: outside these sources, it is also Microsoft's name for personal accounts.

where: Approaches considered (line 56); Sources (lines 36 and 37); Structure item 2 (line 20)
evidence: Brainstorm line 31, the owner's approach: “build the story from what Microsoft said in public (status posts, the executive's root-cause summary)”. Line 56 restates it as “Draft now from Microsoft's own words (chosen by the owner). The service health record gives times to the second and the statements in full”. Line 37 limits X posts to “where the service health record lacks the statement (the apology, the all-clear)”, and line 20 says only “its preliminary cause in one or two plain sentences”. The design never names the executive's root-cause summary (Lamanna, 16 Nov; timeline.json lines 166-172: “Only the opening (search index title) was read”, with the body known only through ITPro, UC Today and HRD America). The backbone is admin-console text: per timeline.json line 419 (gap 2), “The admin-center originals of EX1550543, MO1550821 and TM1550488 need tenant admin sign-in”, so it is not what Microsoft said in public. services.json line 257 put “can the post cite Penn ISC's mirror as Microsoft's own words?” to the owner as Q2, and no answer is recorded. Line 36 decides it anyway: “Cited with Microsoft as the author and the mirror as where it was retrieved.”
fix: Name Lamanna's 16 Nov abridged root cause as a source, to be saved whole from a logged-in browser (ITPro, UC Today and HRD America reproduce parts of it). Say whether the post's cause sentences come from it or from the 14 Nov final status. List services Q2 (cite the mirror as Microsoft's words: A, B or C) as an open question for the owner, and describe the backbone honestly as Microsoft's admin-console text republished by Penn ISC.

evidence: Line 37: “a post is used only where the service health record lacks the statement (the apology, the all-clear)”. The service health record does carry an apology: timeline.json lines 246-253, “Admin-center apology and cause, 17:57:06 UTC, 13 Nov”, whose notes give its opening apology sentence. Disagreement 10 (timeline.json line 418): the admin center says “caused you and your business”, while the @Microsoft X post (16:40:18 UTC) says “caused our customers and partners”.
fix: Limit the parenthetical to the all-clear, and say which apology the post quotes. The record's 17:57:06 UTC wording needs no X capture. The @Microsoft wording is different and does need one, and the post must not mix the two.

evidence: Line 45: “a cost estimate (the only one found, a productivity-loss figure, has no published method, so it is left out)”. The reactions sweep found several: AEG's US$7 billion productivity loss (reactions.json lines 175-181); AEG's refunds of about US$800 million a day (lines 184-190); Morningstar DBRS's US$300m to US$500m in insured losses, CyberCube's under US$100m and Marsh Re's “minimal” (lines 22-28, 193-208); and RMIT's “tens of billions globally” (lines 211-217). Disagreement 7 (line 391) treats them as different quantities, none with a published method. Leaving cost out is the sweep's owner question Q2 (line 392, options A to C), which has no recorded answer, and the owner asked for “how many impact” (brainstorm line 11).
fix: State what was found: several estimates of different quantities (productivity, refunds, insured losses), none with a published method. Put Q2 to the owner as multiple choice instead of deciding it in the design.

evidence: Brainstorm line 29: the owner chose “One login, many doors (Recommended)”, glossed as “the Microsoft services reported down besides mail”, and line 25 has “knowing which work stops when the Microsoft login stops”. Line 32 renames the chart “one account, many doors” and counts “from five services at its first post to twenty in the final status, Exchange Online included”, while line 23 says “Microsoft listed many services beyond mail as impacted (chart 3)”. services.json line 258 counts besides mail, from “4 at 18:27 UTC on 12 Nov” to “19 from 22:00 through the final update”. The design makes three changes (login to account, down to impacted, besides mail to Exchange included) and marks none of them as a departure from the owner's choice.
fix: Count and chart the services besides Exchange Online (4 rising to 19, re-counted by script), or say “including mail” in Section 5 and explain why. List the renaming and the “impacted” label as departures from Q2 and Q6 for the owner to approve.

evidence: Line 15: “(WhatsApp is the natural candidate, especially in Indonesia)”, against line 22: “An example, not an endorsement.” The owner offered WhatsApp as one option among others: “whatsapp or anything that can be use same formal like email” (brainstorm line 13) and “such as WhatsApp” (line 25). Chart 2's own worldwide pair puts email at 76.4% above WhatsApp at 54.9% (reach.json line 213), and WhatsApp is blocked in China (line 28), so “natural” holds for Indonesia, not worldwide. The design also leaves out the one sourced counterpoint from this outage, “HSBC told staff not to use personal email or WhatsApp” (Reuters, reactions.json lines 166-172), and line 40 does not list Reuters.
fix: Use the owner's “such as WhatsApp”, with Indonesia's figure as the reason it fits there. Add HSBC's instruction to Section 4 as a counterpoint the discussion has to answer, and add Reuters (via Euronext Live) to the sources.

evidence: The sweeps put multiple-choice questions to the owner that the brainstorm's eight answers do not cover. services.json line 258, Q1: “which count should the chart show? (A) 19 ... (D) The timestamped step chart”. reactions.json line 392: Q1 “Downdetector numbers in the post”, Q3 “Singapore IPOS excluded-day PDF” and Q4 “Fake-support scams”. The design settles each one without saying so: a step chart that counts Exchange (line 32); “Downdetector figures only as quoted by named outlets”, with no figures named (line 39); IPOS left out; and only the email phishing reported (line 21). The owner asked for every question as multiple choice (brainstorm line 23).
fix: Add an “Open for the owner” list with these questions, plus the mirror and cost questions from the HIGH findings. Give each as multiple choice with the option the design proposes, to be settled at the step 1 checkpoint.

evidence: Line 30: “with Jakarta's Friday working hours marked: the impact window covers them, which is the Indonesia thread's way into the story.” The owner chose “Indonesia comes in where WhatsApp comes up” (brainstorm line 27). The window does cover those hours (23:20 WIB Thursday to 23:10 WIB Friday), but no source defines Jakarta's working hours, so the band's hours would be an unbound figure on the chart. The band also invites the reading that Jakarta lost its working day, while “No Indonesian organisation is named as disrupted” (reactions.json line 343) and the Indonesian onset rests on a single small outlet (lines 346-352).
fix: Keep the Jakarta axis the owner chose, and either drop “the Indonesia thread's way into the story” or put it to the owner. If the band stays, name its hours and their source (not the owner's own hours, which would be a third personal fact), and caption it as Microsoft's global window, not as measured impact in Indonesia.

evidence: Brainstorm line 29: the owner chose “Email vs WhatsApp (Recommended)” for “how many people use each worldwide, with WhatsApp's reach in Indonesia; published user counts, to be verified”. Line 31 charts survey shares instead and says “Counts in billions (Radicati, Meta) are not charted”, without saying that the owner chose counts. It labels the bars “email worldwide, WhatsApp worldwide”, but “GWI covers about 54 markets, not the whole world, and cannot survey Russia” (reach.json line 19). The WhatsApp paragraph “does not name a GWI wave” and its sample “includes China, where WhatsApp is blocked” (line 28), and the sweep asks for the wave and these caveats in a footnote (line 213). Line 38 lists “Internet Use Around the World” (category figures) without saying what it is used for.
fix: Mark the change from counts to shares as a departure from Q6 for the owner to approve. Label the bars “in GWI's surveyed markets” and carry the caveats in the footnote: about 54 markets, China included, Russia excluded, WhatsApp's wave not named. Say what the Internet Use page is for, or drop it.

evidence: Line 31: “No email figure for Indonesia exists on the same basis; the footnote says so”. The sweep searched the reports' text only: “The email-by-country chart is an image, and Indonesia is not named in the text” (reach.json line 19), and “Asking DataReportal or GWI is the only route I can see” (line 212). The footnote would therefore print an absence nobody has verified. Line 22 promises “How many people use email and WhatsApp, worldwide and in Indonesia (chart 2)”, which the chart cannot show for email in Indonesia. The Indonesia WhatsApp value itself “appears only in the chart labels” (line 10), while the gate needs the quote and the value in the stored copy (gate/README.md line 65), and the design does not say how that value will be stored.
fix: In step 2, read the Global Overview's email-by-country chart, and confirm the stored copy of the Indonesia page carries 92.7% as text. Until then, the footnote may say only that neither report's text gives an Indonesia email figure. Reword line 22 to “WhatsApp in Indonesia”.

evidence: Line 32: “as the list grew during the incident (from five services at its first post to twenty in the final status, Exchange Online included)”. The list also shrank: “Defender for Cloud Apps appears as its own entry only at 08:09; Viva Engage appears only at 15:52 and 20:01” (services.json line 13). The series besides mail reads “20 at 08:09; back to 19; 20 at 15:52 and 20:01; 19 from 22:00” (line 258), which makes 21 with Exchange at its peaks, and “22 counting every service ever named” (line 256). Every count “came from a summarizing reader: re-count by script before charting” (line 19). Microsoft's preliminary PIR, as reproduced by Office Watch, lists 14 services including OneDrive, which MO1550821 never names (lines 94-100). Line 62 leaves “the grouping and order on chart 3” to the builder, which fits a list of services rather than a count over time, so the chart's form is unclear.
fix: Describe the list as rising and falling, and state no count until a raw capture has been counted by script. Label the chart “listed as impacted in MO1550821's updates” and footnote the PIR's different list. Say whether chart 3 is a step chart of the count or a timed list of services.

evidence: Line 20: “Microsoft's statement that there was no sign of a cyberattack”. No Microsoft text says this. The final record says the outage was “not related to cyber or AI / agents” (timeline.json lines 264-271, filed as “Statement that it was not a cyberattack, in the final incident record.”). Disagreement 8 (line 418) traces how the wording drifted: “no indication ... malicious activity” at 03:34 UTC, then “not aware” and “no evidence”, then that final sentence and Lamanna's “not a cyberattack”. “No sign of” weakens Microsoft's final position and blends “malicious activity” into “cyberattack”.
fix: Name the statement and the time the post quotes (for example the final status at 04:15:46 UTC on 14 November), and say whether the post mentions the drift.

evidence: Line 20, “its preliminary cause in one or two plain sentences”, does not say which of three cause texts the post uses: 13 Nov, “an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade”; 14 Nov, “traffic shifts ... exposed a latent bug”; or Lamanna's three factors on 16 Nov (disagreement 7, timeline.json line 418). The Preliminary Post-Incident Report itself is admin-only and unread (lines 157-163). Line 57 says “Wait for Microsoft's final post-incident review: its timing is uncertain”, but Microsoft promised a final PIR “within five business days” of 14 Nov (line 262), “reportedly due around 20 Nov 2026” (services.json line 257). The design does not say what happens if that report appears while the post is being drafted.
fix: Name the cause text the post uses (the 14 Nov final status is the stored primary source). Correct the rejected option's reason to Microsoft's five-business-day promise. Add a rule for what to do if the final PIR, or a public copy of it, appears before publication.

evidence: Line 7: “took Outlook mail down for most of a day”. Microsoft's stated impact window is 23 h 50 m (timeline.json lines 183-190), and chart 1 runs about 37.8 hours to the all-clear (line 420). Disagreement 3 (line 418) lists durations from 23 h 50 m to 37 h 50 m, with press figures up to “36-hour”, and at 20:05 UTC on 13 Nov Microsoft still had no ETA for full recovery (lines 121-127). “Most of a day” is shorter than every one of these and names no window, against the design's own rule that the post “says which time it means” (line 51).
fix: Drop the duration from the intent, or tie it to a named window: Microsoft's stated impact window of nearly a day (16:20 UTC on 12 November to 16:10 UTC on 13 November), with the all-clear on 14 November.

evidence: Line 21: “Downdetector's counts, attributed to Downdetector as the outlets quoted them”. The sweep warns that “AP calls them 'users', but Downdetector counts reports” (reactions.json line 37; “These are reports, not people”, line 28), and that “Microsoft gave no number of affected users, mailboxes or regions” (timeline.json line 419, gap 4). On the scams, Microsoft's blog gives no counts and says the available evidence does not confirm credential capture (reactions.json lines 283-289). The design carries none of these limits.
fix: Add them to Section 3: the counts are reports, not users, and AP's word “users” is not repeated; Microsoft gave no figure for affected users; the phishing campaign has no counts and no confirmed credential capture.

evidence: Line 40 lists the reaction sources, “each from its own page”, but none of them supports Section 3's “The joke that it was a day off.” (line 21). The sweep's sources for the joke are CNN via KRDO, the Seattle Times via CPA Practice Advisor and AP via ABC11 (reactions.json lines 175-181, 229-244; “so the trend can be stated”, line 235). Section 4's material on phone and WhatsApp fallbacks beyond the court and the hospital is also unlisted: Reuters on Euronext, Maersk and HSBC (lines 166-172), and AP on meetings moving to WhatsApp (line 238). Workhorse's release was read “as reproduced by Finviz” (lines 121-127), not from its own page.
fix: Add the outlet sources for the joke and for the phone and WhatsApp fallbacks. Record Workhorse's release as read via Finviz until a GlobeNewswire or Workhorse copy is stored.

evidence: Line 36: “The mirror keeps about 30 days, so it is captured in step 2, before mid-December.” The sweeps say “Snapshot the PennO365 page now, before the 30-day window drops these incidents” (timeline.json line 420; “so store a snapshot”, line 181), and they call the drop date uncertain: “may drop off around mid-December 2026 (uncertain). If the post needs a stored primary quote, capture it now” (services.json line 257). The page is “refreshed every 15 minutes” (timeline.json line 181), and its header start time has already changed since 13 Nov (lines 192-199).
fix: Make the raw capture of both incidents, and of the Cloud Admin Hub pages, the first thing done after approval, with no December deadline. Note that a later capture may differ from the one cited.

evidence: Line 30, “Every time comes from the build script reading a data file compiled from the stored records”, does not say whether a script parses that file from the raw capture or someone compiles it by hand. The X times, including chart 1's end at “06:09 UTC on 14 November”, are computed from post IDs, not read off the page (timeline.json line 419, gap 1), and the sweep asks for decode_x_ids.py to be ported “into the repo before publishing any number” (line 420). The design mentions neither. Line 37 allows the all-clear post to be “left out”, but chart 1 ends on that post and the design names no other end point.
fix: State that the build script parses the stored raw captures and decodes the X post IDs with the ported script. Name chart 1's end point for the case where the all-clear post is not saved (for example the final status at 04:15:46 UTC on 14 November).

where: Nowhere in the design (charts, lines 30 to 32; anti-goals, line 46)
evidence: The sweeps name what to keep out, and the design carries none of it. On TM1550488: “Keep it off the Exchange timeline or label it separately” (timeline.json line 289). The services sweep says “Leave out TM1550488 (Microsoft never linked it). Leave out OneDrive except via the PIR, and leave out Azure, Xbox and Entra (news or Downdetector only)”, and allows PP1550869 and CR1551339 a footnote (services.json line 258). The timeline sweep lists the confusable incidents MO1437424, EX1464935, MO1221364 and EX1112414 (timeline.json line 419, gap 7), and EX1464935/MO1465074 of 31 Aug carry the authentication root cause (services.json lines 76-82). With the owner's login point as the turn, that August cause is the most likely wrong import.
fix: Add a line listing these exclusions, and say whether PP1550869 and CR1551339 get the footnote the sweep allows.

evidence: Line 3 says the record is “kept in the session scratchpad as `post31/brainstorm.md` and reproduced in the parts below that rest on them.” The scratchpad lasts only for the session, and several answers are not reproduced faithfully: “Microsoft login” (brainstorm line 25) becomes “Microsoft account”; “One login, many doors” with “reported down besides mail” (line 29) becomes “one account, many doors” with “Exchange Online included”; “published user counts” (line 29) becomes survey shares; and “what Microsoft said in public (status posts, the executive's root-cause summary)” (line 31) becomes the service health record. Line 9 labels the Q1 answer “verbatim” but drops its opening words “In my opinion,” (line 21), which are what mark it as the owner's view (line 33).
fix: Store the brainstorm record in the post's docs/ folder. Either reproduce the eight answers verbatim or remove the claim that they are reproduced, and mark every departure from them as a departure.

evidence: Line 38: “Reuse terms: attribution to DataReportal and its partners with a link”. The terms also require fair dealing and no distortion, ask for an email before ten or more charts are recreated, and do “not say whether you may quote single data points or draw your own chart from them” (reach.json lines 58-64). GWI does not support using its data to criticise another organisation, which “matters if the Outlook outage post frames email figures as criticism of Microsoft” (lines 67-73). The sweep also says “Keep the WhatsApp logo off the chart” (line 208).
fix: Carry these conditions, and the open question on drawing a new chart from the data points, into the rights notes. Add the GWI clause to the anti-goals next to “blaming Microsoft”.

evidence: Line 51 lists “the start: 16:17, 16:20 or 18:26 UTC and a 10:05 UTC header Microsoft never explains” and then says “the post uses Microsoft's own record”. All of these come from Microsoft: “Microsoft's own record gives three different values” (10:05, 16:20, and 16:17 per CIO), and 18:26 is the start of the separate multi-service incident (timeline.json line 418, disagreement 1). The owner's rule was for outlets that disagree with Microsoft (brainstorm line 31), so this constraint does not pick a start.
fix: Name the start: 16:20 UTC, the first EX1550543 post and the start in the final status. Note that 18:26 UTC is when MO1550821 opened, and mention 10:05, if at all, only as unexplained, never as the start (timeline.json line 420).

evidence: Line 15: “while some people took the day as a break”. The owner's fact is that some people “said it was time to take a break” (brainstorm line 33, from line 21), and the public sources report joking (reactions.json line 235), not people actually taking the day off.
fix: Keep “said” (the owner's fact) or use “joked” (the trend the sources report).

evidence: Line 36: “cross-checked with the Cloud Admin Hub mirror”. The sweep matched four items against it (first update, MO 48-hour extension, “approaching normal levels”, final status; timeline.json line 298), and the service lists were read “through WebFetch's summarizing reader” (services.json lines 10, 257). The skill says supporting records, the design included, “make no hand-written claim about when, in what order or how often something was checked” (SKILL.md line 32).
fix: Write “Cloud Admin Hub, a second mirror of the same feed, is the corroborating copy” and leave the checking to the scripts.

evidence: Line 46: “Microsoft reported no identity incident”. The sweep's finding is narrower: “Microsoft names no Entra or sign-in service failure in any 12 to 13 Nov incident I read” (services.json line 256), and that covers only one tenant's view. PP1550869's preliminary root cause is that “a dependency service responsible for authentication was unavailable” (lines 40-46), which a hostile reader could quote.
fix: Narrow the wording: no Microsoft incident read for 12 to 13 November names a sign-in or Entra failure, and PP1550869 and CR1551339 attribute their sign-in failures to Exchange.

evidence: Line 28: “this post has three by the owner's choice (brainstorm, question 6), flagged here as the series rule asks.” The rule allows fewer charts only if “the data genuinely cannot support a fourth honest chart, and flag it” (SKILL.md line 34; line 60). The sweep found a feasible fourth chart, “a dot chart or annotated timeline of Downdetector's own UTC points” (reactions.json line 393), and the owner declined it (brainstorm line 29).
fix: Say that the owner waived the four-chart rule for this post, and that a fourth honest chart existed and was declined.

evidence: Line 52: “Two fact-check rounds at most, then cuts only”. The skill says “a third round needs the owner's ask” (SKILL.md line 63), and the gate requires a round for any surface that did not exist at the last snapshot (gate/README.md lines 90 to 92).
fix: Write “two rounds, then cuts only; a third only on the owner's ask or for a new surface”.

evidence: Design: 'the systems that sit behind a Microsoft account stopped too'. services.json line 10 (MO1550821 notes): 'The impacts are partial: Teams core calls, meetings and chat are said to work, and SharePoint direct file access is said to work. The honest label is impacted, not down.' The design's own chart 3 rule (line 32) says 'never down, because Microsoft describes partial impact on features that depend on Exchange Online'. The thesis states a stop that the design forbids the chart to call 'down', and a hostile reader can quote Microsoft's own Teams and SharePoint lines against it.
fix: Rewrite the thesis to match the record: Microsoft listed other services as impacted, with partial, feature-level impact that depends on Exchange Online. Drop 'stopped' and 'sit behind a Microsoft account'.

evidence: Design line 23: 'The owner's login point. Microsoft listed many services beyond mail as impacted (chart 3). ... which work stops when the Microsoft account stops.' Line 46 anti-goal: 'saying that Microsoft's sign-in service went down (Microsoft reported no identity incident ...)'. services.json line 256, disagreement 6: 'Microsoft names no Entra or sign-in service failure in any 12 to 13 Nov incident I read ... Sign-in as a symptom is Microsoft-backed; sign-in as a failed service is not.' Brainstorm line 25 (Q2): 'knowing which work stops when the Microsoft login stops; ... the owner's login point is the turn of the piece.' The design quietly changes the owner's 'login' to 'account', which is also the name of Microsoft's consumer sign-in. It sets the login point beside chart 3 as if MO1550821 supported it. It never tells the owner that the sources show no login failure in this outage. The flat 'no identity incident' can also be quoted against the post: PP1550869's root cause is 'a dependency service responsible for authentication was unavailable' (services.json line 40).
fix: Raise this with the owner before drafting. State the login point as the owner's general view. For 12 November, say what the record shows: features that depend on Exchange Online, including some sign-ins such as Field Service mobile (CR1551339). Keep the owner's word 'login' unless the owner approves 'account'. Scope the anti-goal to 'no Entra or sign-in service incident in the records read'.

evidence: Design: 'a cost estimate (the only one found, a productivity-loss figure, has no published method, so it is left out)'. reactions.json lines 175 to 217 and line 391 (disagreement 7) list AEG's US$7bn productivity loss, AEG's roughly US$800m a day in refunds, Morningstar DBRS's US$300m to US$500m in insured losses, CyberCube's under US$100m, Marsh Re's 'minimal' and RMIT's 'tens of billions globally'. The sweep also left the cost paragraph as an open owner question (reactions.json line 392, Q2 with options A to C). brainstorm.md records no answer to it.
fix: Correct the reason: there are several estimates, none with a published method, and they measure different quantities. Record the owner's answer to the sweep's cost question before treating cost as cut.

evidence: Design: 'a post is used only where the service health record lacks the statement (the apology, the all-clear)'. timeline.json lines 247 to 253: 'Admin-center apology and cause, 17:57:06 UTC, 13 Nov', with the note 'The same update opens We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused you and your business.' MO1550821 carries it at 17:57:20 UTC. So the record does contain the apology. Section 2's event list (line 20) does not include the apology at all, so where it goes in the post is unplanned.
fix: Take the apology from the record (17:57:06 UTC, 'caused you and your business') and note that the X wording differs (timeline disagreement 10). Use X only for the all-clear. Either add the apology to section 2's list or say it is cut.

evidence: Brainstorm line 31: 'build the story from what Microsoft said in public (status posts, the executive's root-cause summary)'. Design line 56: 'Draft now from Microsoft's own words (chosen by the owner). The service health record gives times to the second'. The design's backbone is the tenant admin record, read through a third-party mirror (line 36). Per services.json line 28, epifive says the patch wording was 'in the admin-center posts only, not on the public status page or @MSFT365Status'. Whether the post may cite that mirror as Microsoft's own words is an open owner question (services.json line 257, Q2 with options A to C), and brainstorm.md records no answer. The executive's root-cause summary (Lamanna, 16 Nov; timeline.json lines 166 to 172, body known only through ITPro, UC Today and HRD) appears nowhere in the plan. Section 2's 'its preliminary cause' does not say which of three framings it means (timeline.json line 418, disagreement 7: the 13 Nov capacity upgrade, the 14 Nov latent bug, or the 16 Nov three factors).
fix: Record the owner's answer on citing the mirror. Say whether the executive's root-cause summary is used, and from which stored copy, or tell the owner it is dropped. Name the cause statement section 2 uses, with its time.

evidence: Brainstorm line 29 (Q6): 'Email vs WhatsApp (Recommended) (how many people use each worldwide, with WhatsApp's reach in Indonesia; published user counts, to be verified)'. Design line 31 charts 'the share of internet users aged 16 and over' and says 'Counts in billions (Radicati, Meta) are not charted'. The change of measure is not flagged as a departure from the owner's choice. Section 4 (line 22) still promises 'How many people use email and WhatsApp, worldwide and in Indonesia (chart 2)', although chart 2 has no counts and no Indonesia email bar.
fix: Flag the switch from user counts to survey shares as a change that needs the owner's approval; reach.json line 213 gives the reason and options A to D. Reword section 4 to 'what share of internet users use each', and drop Indonesia for email.

evidence: Design: 'to the all-clear posted on X (06:09 UTC on 14 November)' and 'Every time comes from the build script reading a data file compiled from the stored records'. Line 37 says X posts are 'saved from a logged-in browser with the owner's agreement, or left out'. timeline.json line 419 (gaps 1): 'Every X time here is computed from the post ID (snowflake ...), not read off the page'. timeline.json line 420 says to port decode_x_ids.py 'into the repo before publishing any number'. The design gives no endpoint if the X post is left out, yet the owner's chart runs 'to the all-clear' (brainstorm line 29). It does not say the data file is extracted by a script rather than typed. It also does not say whether chart 1 mixes EX1550543, MO1550821 and X times; the 48-hour extension, for example, is at 09:03:36 (MO), 09:24:08 (X) and 09:55:42 (EX).
fix: Name the stored artifact each plotted time comes from, extract every time with a script (plus the ported decode script for X IDs), and pick one track per event. Give the owner a fallback endpoint, such as the final status at 04:15:46 UTC, noting that it still says restoration continues.

evidence: Design: 'every figure and quote is bound through docs/sources.json'. SKILL.md line 38: 'The quote must occur exactly once in the stored document'. The stored Penn page (about 893,000 characters, timeline.json line 181) holds EX1550543 and MO1550821 together, and key sentences repeat. The final status's start and end window appears in both EX (04:15:46) and MO (04:17:52) (timeline.json line 187). 'Approaching normal levels' appears at 14:01:18 in EX and 14:01:51 in MO (line 100). 'This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents.' appears at 17:57:06 and 04:15:46 (line 268). For chart 2, reach.json line 10 says the Indonesia WhatsApp value 'appears only in the chart labels'.
fix: Plan the stored documents so each bound quote is unique: use longer quotes that carry the incident ID or timestamp, or store a copy per incident. Before committing chart 2's Indonesia bar, confirm the value appears as text in the stored DataReportal copy.

evidence: Design: 'as the list grew during the incident (from five services at its first post to twenty in the final status, Exchange Online included)'. services.json line 13: 'Defender for Cloud Apps appears as its own entry only at 08:09; Viva Engage appears only at 15:52 and 20:01.
